AI-worker goals and regression evidence

Bounded work. Independent proof. Cumulative feature protection.

A decomposition of the existing roadmap, not a claim that the application has been built.
190Worker goals

151 / 151Requirements mapped
All application tests are not run. The package contains executable planning/inventory helper self-tests, separate from the proposed product tests. Source-system qualification, human decisions and actual pilot observations cannot be replaced with simulated success.

Start with M00-G01. Give each worker one packet after its dependencies are accepted. Use the installed git-agent workflow, ordinary project commands and one writer per isolated worktree. Every accepted feature adds protected regression obligations.

M00 — Product charter and reproducible development

Establish a buildable project and an accepted product boundary before implementation becomes a collection of unrelated agent experiments.

M00-G01 · Freeze the first-release support envelope
governancenormal riskhuman_decisionnot started

Outcome: Create versioned charter and capability/support-envelope records naming first customer, Shopify-first/WooCommerce-second scope, actions, payment/fulfillment exclusions and release claims; obtain human approval.

Depends on: No prior goal; obtain the actual charter decision.

Owned scope: charter/ADRs/support-envelope; planning schemas and validation fixtures. Proposed modules; bind to real repository paths.

Required tests and independent oracles

CASE-M00-G01-01 · positive

Arrange / act: Validate a named supported order-status and return scenario against the approved matrix

Assert: Every scenario resolves to a supported, conditional or explicitly excluded capability with a reason and accountable owner.

CASE-M00-G01-02 · negative

Arrange / act: Introduce a refund/payment combination absent from the envelope

Assert: Validation rejects an automatic supported label and requires a reviewed scope decision.

CASE-M00-G01-03 · regression

Arrange / act: Remove an already accepted capability from the matrix

Assert: Baseline comparison detects the removal and blocks an unchanged release claim.

Broken behavior to detect: Delete one accepted capability row while keeping its advertised release claim.

Evidence and acceptance

  • manifest.json: candidate/base SHA, source-tree/build digests, config/skill/policy/model/adapter pins, environment, fixture hashes and actual timestamps.
  • tests/native-report.* and tests/results.json: exact commands/exit codes, discovered and executed stable case IDs, totals and native report hashes; zero-test/skip/todo is not pass.
  • red-green.md: observed behavioral red failure or valid targeted mutant failure, repaired-candidate pass, and the exact code/config change that caused each outcome.
  • demo.md plus sanitized API trace or UI recording: demonstrate the named outcome on this candidate; screenshots alone do not establish money or stock correctness.
  • regression-review.md: compare accepted capability/test baseline, changed/deleted tests and oracle files, compatibility, migrations and old journeys; independent reviewer decision.
  • security-review.md: independent authority/tenant/secret/side-effect review proportional to risk; no self-approval for critical changes.
  • handoff.md: implementation paths, actual commands, remaining limits, rollback/recovery, deployment/support implications and next unblocked goals.
  • decision.json: trusted integration owner/maintainer acceptance is separate from author evidence; public/tagged release requires human authorization.
  • Human-approved charter; capability matrix; decision record; checks over supported and excluded fixtures.

Preserve: Run own tests plus all accepted tests impacted by this change, all introduced cross-cutting invariants, and the deterministic regression suite. Milestone/release candidate runs the full applicable accepted suite and required connected qualification.

CASE-M05-G99-01 · positive

Assert: Every in-scope goal and original exit criterion has current evidence; the cumulative suite has nonzero executed counts and no skipped mandatory cases.

CASE-M05-G99-02 · negative

Arrange / act: A component passes in isolation but breaks an earlier capability, lacks connected proof, uses stale evidence or contains an unapproved scope exclusion

Assert: The integration gate rejects acceptance and lists the exact missing obligations.

CASE-M05-G99-03 · regression

Assert: Trusted-baseline and behavior-specific regression checks fail; after repair, rerun the integrated candidate and refresh reviews.

Broken behavior to detect: Delete one previously accepted scenario or disable an older feature while retaining the new milestone demo.

Evidence and acceptance

  • manifest.json: candidate/base SHA, source-tree/build digests, config/skill/policy/model/adapter pins, environment, fixture hashes and actual timestamps.

  • demo.md plus sanitized API trace or UI recording: demonstrate the named outcome on this candidate; screenshots alone do not establish money or stock correctness.

  • handoff.md: implementation paths, actual commands, remaining limits, rollback/recovery, deployment/support implications and next unblocked goals.
  • decision.json: trusted integration owner/maintainer acceptance is separate from author evidence; public/tagged release requires human authorization.
  • Original required demo: Resolve a tracking query, process an approved return, hand off an exception and disable the model while the operator continues the same case. Capture exact commit/build/configuration, cumulative reports, independent reviews and maintainer decision. Tagged/public release needs human approval.

Preserve: Run own tests plus all accepted tests impacted by this change, all introduced cross-cutting invariants, and the deterministic regression suite. Milestone/release candidate runs the full applicable accepted suite and required connected qualification.

Original milestone exit criteria

  • Human takeover stops further agent actions without losing case context; new messages in other channels do not bypass customer verification.
  • Verified policy answers and completed business actions are measured separately from attempts; all sampled financial outcomes reconcile.
  • Provider outage or budget exhaustion falls back to queued/manual operation; no new provider receives customer data without merchant approval.
  • Opt-out arriving concurrently with a scheduled marketing message suppresses the send; transactional behavior follows configured consent/policy rules.
